subject: Chemistry
title: Lavoisier: Chemistry Gets Precise
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Lavoisier: Chemistry Gets Precise.

hook.text: Antoine Lavoisier weighed everything. He proved that mass is conserved in reactions—ending phlogiston theory.

buildup.text: Before Lavoisier, chemists thought burning released a substance called 'phlogiston.' He showed it absorbed oxygen instead.

discovery.text: By careful measurement, he proved that the total mass before and after a reaction is always the same.

twist.text: He named oxygen and hydrogen, wrote the first modern chemistry textbook, and created the first systematic nomenclature.

climax.text: During the French Revolution, he was guillotined. The judge said: 'The Republic has no need of scientists.'

punchline.text: Weighed every reaction, named the elements, lost his head. Chemistry's tragic hero.

quiz.question: What key principle did Lavoisier establish by weighing reactions?
options: Conservation of mass—total mass stays the same before and after a reaction
Energy cannot be created or destroyed
All elements have a fixed atomic weight

details.summary: Antoine Lavoisier used precise mass measurements to prove that chemical reactions conserve mass, establishing the law of conservation of mass..
details.whyItMatters: Lavoisier is called the father of modern chemistry. His emphasis on quantitative measurement, systematic nomenclature, and theoretical rigor completed the transformation of alchemy into an exact science.
takeaways: Lavoisier proved that mass is conserved in all chemical reactions
He identified oxygen as the element responsible for combustion
His systematic nomenclature replaced confusing alchemical terminology

faq.question: How did Lavoisier disprove the phlogiston theory?
faq.answer: Phlogiston theory claimed burning released an invisible substance. Lavoisier showed that combustion required a specific gas he named oxygen and that the total mass of reactants and products remained constant..

faq.question: Why was Lavoisier executed during the French Revolution?
faq.answer: Lavoisier was a tax collector for the Ancien Régime through the Ferme Générale, which was deeply hated by the French public. Despite his scientific contributions, he was arrested, tried, and guillotined in 1794 during the Reign of Terror..
